MSFT.headline: Texas restarts data center permits, but it is too early to drop the FY28 haircut
paragraphs: The Texas environmental regulator says it has resumed normal review of data center air permits, ending the pause Governor Abbott ordered in September (Texas Tribune, article read). This touches our FY28 one point growth haircut for Texas and Wyoming permitting, but we would not remove it yet. The grid operator's final audit report is only due December 10, the article does not say the separate pause on grid connections has ended, and the governor-elect campaigned on keeping approvals paused until new laws pass.

The ByteDance story moved from report to politics. The chair of the House China committee said on the record that Microsoft should not sell AI services to ByteDance and asked for a briefing (Reuters), while the roughly $500 million Azure deal is still only reported by The Information and Microsoft has not commented. No export rule or legal step exists today, so Intelligent Cloud revenue growth is unchanged, but the risk to Chinese demand for OpenAI models on Azure is more visible.

Two items are loud but do not change the model. Microsoft and Intel confirmed a long-term agreement for multi-year Xeon supply and Intel packaging for Azure's own chips, with no dollar amounts, volumes or dates, so capex and cost of revenue stay as they are. On the Outlook outage, headlines say Nadella apologized and customers can request credits (CNBC and Variety, headlines only, articles not read), which would touch Productivity revenue growth and operating margin, but nobody has sized them.
watch: December 10 ERCOT final report and December 17 Texas utility commission meeting, plus what the governor-elect does with permits in January
Whether Microsoft answers the House China committee, and any move to restrict selling US AI models to Chinese firms through the cloud
Any Microsoft figure for outage credits, and the reported Canadian class actions (headline only)
MSFT.note: Confirmed by the companies: the Intel agreement (joint press release). On the record: the Texas regulator and the House committee chair. Reported only: the ByteDance deal and its size. Outage details and a UK cloud probe headline were not verified, and the UK item may be an old story.
